Bank and Slope Stabilization

Flexible Concrete Revetment™

Strength without behaving like a rigid slab.

A site-specific concrete revetment system designed to protect steep banks, head cuts, channels and slopes while flexing under changing loads and relieving hydrostatic pressure.

Does this look familiar?

The slope is failing faster than surface repairs can hold.

FCR may be considered where steep grades, head cuts, runoff or changing water levels are eroding a slope or bank. These sites often need substantial protection that can accommodate movement and water pressure rather than fighting both as a rigid mass.

Active Head Cuts

Erosion progressing upstream and continuing to deepen the channel.

Steep or Confined Slopes

Limited room and critical infrastructure increasing the consequence of failure.

Recurring High Flow

Repeated events removing soil and undermining earlier repairs.

How FCR works

Protect the surface while allowing the system to respond.

FCR is engineered around the site and installed as a connected concrete protection system. Its configuration distributes erosive forces across the protected area while retaining the ability to flex as the underlying conditions change.

The system is also designed to relieve hydrostatic pressure. That combination can provide a more durable response in places where rigid concrete may be vulnerable to cracking, uplift or separation.

  1. 01
    Evaluate the Failure

    Identify slope geometry, runoff, flow paths, soils, groundwater and the progression of erosion.

  2. 02
    Design the Revetment

    Set the limits, thickness, anchoring and configuration required for the site.

  3. 03
    Prepare and Install

    Shape the protected area, place the system and complete the designed anchoring.

  4. 04
    Restore the Site

    Finish transitions, drainage and surrounding contours so the system works with the broader site.

Why flexibility matters

A durable surface still needs to respond to the site.

Handles Steep Grades

Provides substantial protection where erosion is concentrated along difficult slopes.

Manages Uplift

Pressure relief helps reduce forces created by trapped water beneath the protection.

Accommodates Movement

A connected flexible system can respond where a single rigid surface may be challenged.

Integrates with the Site

Terraces, vegetation zones and project-specific transitions can be incorporated where appropriate.

The goal is not an online diagnosis

It is a better first conversation.

If a steep bank, channel or head cut continues to fail, send us the location, field photos and any available plans or drainage information. Er-Con will evaluate the cause and whether FCR or another stabilization approach fits the site.

Seeing something similar?

Tell us what is happening at the site.
